questions.explanation: Instruments take 'the': play the piano.

questions.q: ___ people I met there were very friendly.
questions.explanation: A defining relative clause makes the noun specific, so use 'the'.
No article with 'in prison' meaning as a prisoner.

options: The rich should help the poor.
A rich should help a poor.
The rich should help a poor.
questions.explanation: Adjectives for groups of people take 'the'.
'Few' (not many) stresses the small number negatively.
'Little' with uncountable nouns stresses almost none.

options: The unemployed need more support from the government.
Unemployed need more support from the government.
An unemployed need more support from the government.
The unemployeds need more support from the government.
questions.explanation: Groups described by adjectives take 'the'.

questions.q: ___ Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
questions.explanation: Mountain names take no article.
'Advice' is uncountable, so use 'some', not 'a'.

options: She has a little close friends she can trust.
She has a few close friends she can trust.
She has few close friends she can trust.
She has the few close friends she can trust.
questions.explanation: 'A few' with countable nouns means a small but positive number.
Uncountable nouns in general statements take no article.

questions.q: There's ___ milk left — just enough for coffee.
questions.explanation: 'A little' with uncountable nouns means a small but enough amount.

options: They travelled by train across Europe.
They travelled by the train across Europe.
They travelled by a train across Europe.
They travelled with train across Europe.
questions.explanation: 'By + transport' takes no article.

questions.q: Only ___ students passed — the exam was very hard.
questions.explanation: 'Only a few' stresses a surprisingly small number positively.

questions.q: It was ___ interesting book that I read it twice.
questions.explanation: 'Such + a/an + adjective + noun' expresses degree.

options: The life is too short to waste time.
A life is too short to waste time.
Life is too short to waste the time.
Life is too short to waste time.
questions.explanation: Abstract nouns in general statements take no article.
'The news' refers to the news as a known concept.

questions.q: She has ___ experience for this job.
questions.explanation: 'Little experience' stresses not enough for the job.

options: The half class was absent yesterday.
Half of class was absent yesterday.
A half the class was absent yesterday.
Half the class was absent yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Half the class' needs no 'of' before 'the'.

questions.q: He earns ___ money, but he's happy.
questions.explanation: 'Little money' stresses the small amount negatively.
